methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: This research addresses the need for integration concepts, holistic monitoring and analysis methodologies, life-cycle oriented decision support and scenario based control strategies through the seamless integration of ubiquitous sensing infrastructures, simulation tools, BIM tools, service oriented architectures and data warehouse technologies.

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Presents an integrated IT system architecture (wireless sensing, eeBIM, ETL, data warehouse/OLAP, monitoring GUIs, intelligent control) for building energy monitoring and optimisation, but does not identify or characterise an EnPI/EnB measurement model -- no normalisation variables, functional form, or baseline construction/estimation approach is given (building performance is only 'simulated using the energy simulation tool EIS'). Tool/software-design paper without EnPI/EnB model content.

paper_type.evidence_quote: The developed system architecture covers the implementation of a modular platform as depicted in Figure 1, that integrates multiple dimensions of building information such as performance data

stage1.notes: Identity confirmed via ISBN 978-0-415-62128-1 (identity_override; printed title differs from Rayyan title). Context is a residential HDA building in Istanbul -> buildings are out of scope for 3B. Borderline: monitoring compares actual vs intended (simulated) performance, but no EnPI/EnB model is characterised.
